module_title: Visual vs. Performing Arts, Indigenous Games & EBSB Integration
introduction: This intermediate tier explores the practical implementation of AIL and SIL in classrooms. It distinguishes between Visual and Performing arts, highlights the use of indigenous Indian games, and details the Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat (EBSB) mandate for CBSE schools.

core_concepts.title: Forms of Art Integration
core_concepts.description:
Teachers can utilize two broad categories of art:
1. Visual Arts: Drawing, painting, clay modeling, paper crafts, and photography. (e.g., Using origami to teach symmetry and 3D shapes).
2. Performing Arts: Music, dance, theatre, role-play, and puppetry. (e.g., Using a socio-dramatic role-play to understand the Dandi March in History, fostering deep empathy and historical inquiry).

core_concepts.title: Indigenous Sports and Local Context
core_concepts.description:
NCF-SE 2023 places heavy emphasis on integrating **indigenous games** (e.g., Kabaddi, Kho-Kho, Pachisi, Pallanguzhi, Lattu/Top) rather than just Western sports.
- Pedagogical Value: Indigenous games are deeply rooted in local culture, require zero to low-cost equipment, and naturally integrate math (counting, geometry of the field) and physics (momentum, balance).

core_concepts.title: Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat (EBSB) Mandate
core_concepts.description:
A major initiative by the Government of India, strictly integrated into CBSE’s AIL guidelines.
- Concept: States and Union Territories are paired together (e.g., Delhi is paired with Sikkim). 
- Application: Students must complete Art-Integrated Projects where they research and create art based on the culture, flora, fauna, or history of their *paired state*. This promotes national integration, cultural appreciation, and multidisciplinary research.

core_concepts.title: Cross-Curricular Linkages
core_concepts.description:
A single art or sport activity can map to multiple subjects simultaneously.
- Example: Designing a kite. 
  - Math: Measuring dimensions and calculating surface area.
  - Science: Understanding aerodynamics, wind pressure, and material weight.
  - Art: Decorating with symmetrical cultural motifs.

important_entities.name: CBSE Circular on AIL
important_entities.key_fact: Art-Integrated Projects are mandatory for Classes 1 to 10.
important_entities.significance: CBSE made it compulsory that every student in Classes 1-10 must undertake at least one Art-Integrated Project per subject per year, and for Classes 1-8, at least one of these projects must be under the Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat (EBSB) pairing.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A common misconception is that play, art, and sports integration are only for foundational/primary stages. **FALSE**. NEP 2020 explicitly states that AIL and SIL must be utilized across ALL stages, including Middle and Secondary, to teach complex multidisciplinary concepts.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat is all about *Pairing* states to *Share* cultural art and knowledge.

exam_strategy_tips: If an exam asks 'What is the primary objective of pairing states under the EBSB program for art projects?', select the option related to **promoting national integration and mutual understanding of diverse cultures**.
